changeSet.author: fineract
changeSet.comment: FINERACT-2797: persist whether a savings account transaction was created through the "Force Withdrawal" command (FINERACT-2471), so future balance re-validations can recognize a historical negative-balance excursion as legitimately authorized, instead of relying solely on the caller context of a later, unrelated transaction.

changeSet.author: fineract
changeSet.comment: Backfill is_force_transaction=true for pre-existing force-withdrawal transactions, identified via the audit trail (m_portfolio_command_source) since the flag did not exist at the time those transactions were originally created. The command returns the withdrawal id as its resource id: rows that have result_ids_written hold it in result_resource_id, older rows hold it in resource_id (they were overwritten with the result), and rows that kept the submitted ids but have no result yet hold the savings account id there, so they are skipped.
changeSet.sql: UPDATE m_savings_account_transaction SET is_force_transaction = true WHERE is_force_transaction = false AND transaction_type_enum = 2 AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM m_portfolio_command_source cs WHERE cs.action_name = 'FORCE_WITHDRAWAL' AND cs.entity_name = 'SAVINGSACCOUNT' AND cs.savings_account_id = m_savings_account_transaction.savings_account_id AND m_savings_account_transaction.id = CASE WHEN cs.result_ids_written = true THEN cs.result_resource_id WHEN cs.submitted_ids_kept = true THEN NULL ELSE cs.resource_id END);

changeSet.author: fineract
changeSet.comment: Backfill the copies of forced withdrawals. When a balance recalculation (interest posting, back-dated transaction) changed the overdraft amount of a forced withdrawal, it reversed the withdrawal and inserted a copy with a new id, which the audit trail does not know. The copy keeps the account, type, date and amount of the reversed original, and is inserted after it.
changeSet.sql: UPDATE m_savings_account_transaction copy_tx SET is_force_transaction = true FROM m_savings_account_transaction forced_tx WHERE copy_tx.savings_account_id = forced_tx.savings_account_id AND copy_tx.transaction_type_enum = forced_tx.transaction_type_enum AND copy_tx.transaction_date = forced_tx.transaction_date AND copy_tx.amount = forced_tx.amount AND copy_tx.id > forced_tx.id AND forced_tx.is_force_transaction = true AND forced_tx.is_reversed = true AND forced_tx.is_reversal = false AND copy_tx.is_force_transaction = false AND copy_tx.is_reversal = false;

changeSet.author: fineract
changeSet.comment: Same backfill as the PostgreSQL changeset above, written as a multi-table update because MySQL cannot select from the table it updates in a subquery.
changeSet.sql: UPDATE m_savings_account_transaction copy_tx JOIN m_savings_account_transaction forced_tx ON copy_tx.savings_account_id = forced_tx.savings_account_id AND copy_tx.transaction_type_enum = forced_tx.transaction_type_enum AND copy_tx.transaction_date = forced_tx.transaction_date AND copy_tx.amount = forced_tx.amount AND copy_tx.id > forced_tx.id SET copy_tx.is_force_transaction = true WHERE forced_tx.is_force_transaction = true AND forced_tx.is_reversed = true AND forced_tx.is_reversal = false AND copy_tx.is_force_transaction = false AND copy_tx.is_reversal = false;
